Tools

Engineering tools for the liquid loop

Each tool does one thing a thermal engineer would otherwise do on the back of an envelope, and states the assumptions it makes. Use them to sharpen a question before you bring it to us or to anyone else.

01

Liquid cooling simulator

Transient thermal model of the whole loop, from chip junction to heat rejection: pick a rack platform, climate and pipework, then watch junction temperature, flow, pressure drop and pPUE settle, and stress it with load steps, pump loss or fouling. Includes pipe sizing and a 3D view.

Open sim.nextgenergy.ai →02

CDU catalog

Public specifications for coolant distribution units from more than thirty vendors, each row linked to the vendor datasheet, with the rating conditions shown next to the capacity so the numbers can actually be compared.

Open →
03

Return-water grade → feasible heat buyers

Enter the temperature your loop returns at. See which off-takers can physically use the heat, which need a heat-pump lift, and roughly how much.

Open →04

Approach temperature → CDU sizing

See how the approach across the CDU heat exchanger moves facility supply temperature, and what that does to free-cooling hours in your climate.

Open →05

Turnover self-check

Ten boundaries, three questions each. Score a project honestly and get a number you can compare next time.
